# **Main Questions**
***

The Motivation section introduced the central puzzle: each {{< glossary "Peripheral blood mononuclear cell" display="PBMC" >}} carries {{< glossary "Immune-cell identity" display="immune-cell identity" >}}, donor context, and {{< glossary "IFN-beta" display="IFN-beta" >}} response information at the same time. The questions below turn that puzzle into an analysis path. You will first inspect what {{< glossary "CoGAPS" display="CoGAPS" >}} learns from control and IFN-beta-stimulated cells, then ask whether the learned {{< glossary "Latent pattern" display="patterns" >}} separate broad {{< glossary "Stimulation-associated activity" display="stimulation activity" >}} from {{< glossary "Cell-type-linked pattern" display="cell-type-linked structure" >}}, which genes support the {{< glossary "IFN-associated pattern" display="IFN-associated interpretation" >}}, and how that pattern varies across annotated PBMC cell types.

:::{.main_question}
::::{.main_question_header}
Our main questions
::::
::::{.inner_block}
1. What {{< glossary "Latent pattern" display="latent transcriptional programs" >}} are present in IFN-beta stimulated and control PBMC {{< glossary "Single-cell RNA-seq" display="single-cell RNA-seq" >}} data?
1. Can CoGAPS help distinguish broad {{< glossary "Stimulation-associated activity" display="stimulation-associated activity" >}} from {{< glossary "Cell-type-linked pattern" display="cell-type-linked immune programs" >}}?
1. Which genes define the strongest {{< glossary "IFN-associated pattern" display="IFN-associated pattern" >}}, and what is their {{< glossary "Directionality" display="direction" >}} in stimulation?
1. How does the IFN-associated pattern vary across annotated PBMC cell types?
::::
:::

<td><strong>Question 1</strong><br>What latent transcriptional programs are present in IFN-beta stimulated and control PBMC single-cell RNA-seq data?</td>
<td><strong>Data Import</strong> introduces the teaching PBMC dataset and the saved CoGAPS results used for the main analysis. <strong>Data Exploration</strong>, <strong>Data Visualization</strong>, and <strong>Data Analysis</strong> then inspect the learned gene weights, cell activities, and pattern summaries.</td>
<td>CoGAPS represents the PBMC data as multiple latent transcriptional patterns rather than one label per cell. Those patterns become the signals you will interpret in later sections.</td>
</tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
<td><img src="img/question_icons/rq2_shared_vs_celltype.png" alt="Icon showing a CoGAPS analysis splitting into one shared activity band across cell types and separate cell-type-specific program panels." width="130"></td>
<td><strong>Question 2</strong><br>Can CoGAPS help distinguish broad stimulation-associated activity from cell-type-linked immune programs?</td>
<td><strong>Data Exploration</strong> and <strong>Data Visualization</strong> show how cells are grouped by condition and cell type. <strong>Data Analysis</strong> compares how strongly each pattern follows stimulation, which genes define it, and where its activity is strongest across labeled cell types.</td>
<td>A useful model should help separate a broad stimulation-associated activity signal from patterns that look more cell-type-linked or mixed.</td>
</tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
<td><img src="img/question_icons/rq3_ifn_genes_directionality.png" alt="Icon showing IFN signaling into a cell, a highlighted pattern module, and a ranked red and blue gene list for up- and down-direction genes." width="130"></td>
<td><strong>Question 3</strong><br>Which genes define the strongest IFN-associated pattern, and what is their direction in stimulation?</td>
<td><strong>Data Visualization</strong> previews how top pattern genes can be paired with expression direction. <strong>Data Analysis</strong> identifies the IFN-associated pattern from cell activities, ranks its top genes, and checks whether those genes are higher or lower in IFN-beta-stimulated cells.</td>
<td>The IFN-associated interpretation should be supported by canonical {{< glossary "Interferon-stimulated gene" display="interferon-stimulated genes" >}}, and {{< glossary "Gene weight" display="gene weights" >}} must be interpreted alongside directionality.</td>
</tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
<td><img src="img/question_icons/rq4_ifn_activity_by_celltype.png" alt="Icon showing an IFN-associated pattern branching into multiple PBMC cell-type rows with distinct mini expression profiles." width="130"></td>
<td><strong>Question 4</strong><br>How does the IFN-associated pattern vary across annotated PBMC cell types?</td>
<td><strong>Data Visualization</strong> previews IFN-associated activity by cell type and condition. <strong>Data Analysis</strong> compares the pattern across labeled PBMC cell types and checks whether the same gene-direction story appears within those groups.</td>
<td>The IFN-associated pattern should be read as broad but not uniform: its cell activity can cut across immune-cell identities while still varying in strength across cell types.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The questions are ordered intentionally. First you inspect the latent patterns that CoGAPS learns. Then you separate shared stimulation structure from cell-type-linked structure. Only after that do you attach biological meaning through top genes, directionality, and cell-type summaries.
